100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 17, 1926, the United States faced a severe drought that continued to devastate agricultural regions, causing concern over food supplies and economic stability. In Europe, tensions escalated as the League of Nations convened to address the ongoing crisis in the Ruhr Valley, where French and Belgian troops maintained a contentious occupation. Meanwhile, the British government grappled with labor unrest, as workers demanded better wages amid rising costs of living.
